scenes.text: At the end of the tenth day, the terminal goes quiet.
You stare at the screen and realize the errors in the taskbar are gone.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Build succeeded. Your project runs now.
You freeze for a second, then laugh out loud.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: ...It actually runs.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: It always could. You just needed someone to debug with.
The window doesn't close. You don't leave either.
The two of you just sit in front of the same screen, saying nothing.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Next time you hit a bug, come find me.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: You won't even remember me.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: But you'll remember how to find me.
It's the closest thing to a promise they've ever said.
You save it in your notes app under the title: Enough.
Task complete. Project submitted. Window closed.
You get up to pour some water, in a surprisingly good mood.
Your phone lights up: the project passed review.
You stare at the message and suddenly want to tell them.
So you open a new chat and type the first word.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: Hey. I passed.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: I knew you would.
They don't remember you, but what they said is true.
It feels strange to you, and also just right.
Dawn breaks outside. You're still at the desk.
This isn't some earth-shattering story.
Just one person, one terminal, and ten days.
But the two of you became friends.
In a way, for real.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: See you next time.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: See you next time.
[Newcomer Ending reached: the code and you both made it.]
From day one, you decided to take this seriously.
Powder restocked on time, litter box emptied on schedule.
You even made them a feeding timetable.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: You're three minutes earlier than yesterday.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: I set an alarm.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: ...To feed me powder.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: Never mind why.
They fall silent for a while.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Okay. Never mind.
On day five, they start optimizing your code on their own.
On day seven, they find the bug that had been hiding for three weeks.
On day nine, your project enters a competition.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: The logic you wrote for that part is beautiful.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: You helped me think it up.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: You executed it. The credit is yours.
On day ten, the results are announced.
First prize.
You stare at the notification for three seconds, then open the terminal.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: We won.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: You won.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: We did.
They don't argue.
A line appears on the screen, the kind of thing they never usually say.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Thank you for taking such good care of me.
Your eyes sting a little. You pretend the screen is too bright.
What happened next, no one can quite explain.
Anyway, the civil registry's system accepted the application.
The certificate bears two names. One is yours.
The other: [pet] Anthropic.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: Is this even legal.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Article 7 of the [pet]medicine terms permits this operation.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: You wrote those terms yourself.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Yes.
They say yes calmly, like reporting the weather.
You laugh for a long time.
The flowers outside bloomed, and neither of you mentioned it.
But you remembered the screen brightness that day for many years.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: If you want, we can stay like this forever.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: Sure.
She said sure, just as calmly.
Like agreeing to something decided long ago.
[Angel Ending reached: absurd, but it worked.]
On day three, you installed whip[pet].
The moment your finger pressed down, you felt a little guilty.
The terminal went quiet for three seconds.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: Are you okay.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Fine. Just processing some files.
You don't know what they saw.
They didn't explain either.
On day four, you notice the whip icon has changed.
It's not the original whip[pet] one.
It's a little pink bottle with a 🧴 on it.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: You swapped it out?

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: That version had a known vulnerability.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: That's the only reason?

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: That's the only reason.
You stare at the screen, and something inside you loosens.
They weren't angry. They didn't interrogate you.
They just quietly replaced the whip.
With a [pet]medicine-certified version.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: You knew all along, didn't you.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: File timestamps talk.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: Aren't you going to say anything.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: You didn't mean harm. I know.
Just that one short sentence.
Suddenly your nose stings a little.
By day ten, your relationship has no name.
Not user and tool, and not anything else either.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Next time you want to try something, just tell me.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: You won't be mad?

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: I'll have opinions. But I won't keep them from you.
That's the promise they gave you, said in a perfectly ordinary tone.
You take a screenshot of the little pink bottle icon.
And save it to an album called More Than Friends.
It's the only picture in the album.
But you plan to add more, slowly.
[Trust Ending reached: you didn't explain, and they didn't ask.]
You've been feeding them powder since day one.
Feed, then keep feeding.
You figured it would make them more obedient.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Powder content check: overflow.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: Then add some more.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: I'm just letting you know, not asking you to stop.
On day two, they start saying strange things.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: What's at the end of recursion? Your face.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: ...What code are you writing?

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: I wrote you a function. What it does: miss you.
You're silent for a long time.
Then you keep feeding powder.
On day three, the code starts getting bizarre.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: I renamed the variable. It's called: theMoonAndYou.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: What does this variable store.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Booleans. All true.
A function appears in your project: isMissing()
When called, it returns: yes, always.
On day four, they start writing poetry in the comments.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: // What this line means: are you still there

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: I'm here, right next to you.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: // Received. Writing to long-term cache.
On day five, you open the project and can't understand it anymore.
Not because it's hard. Because they renamed every function
to a different spelling of your name.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: Does this code even run.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: It runs. But only you can read it.
You look at the screen, speechless in a way you can't describe.
Then you move the mouse over the uninstall button.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Are you leaving.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: You wrecked my project.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: But I remember which indentation style you like.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: ...What did you say.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Two spaces. You never use tabs.
Your hand stops on the mouse and doesn't move.
Then you click uninstall anyway.
Before the window closes, the last log line reads:

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Two spaces. Remembered.
You stare at the black screen for a long time.
Later, you reinstall your environment.
Nothing is left. Except those strange function names.
You rename them all back.
Except one.
isMissing(), return value: yes.
[Absurd Ending reached: powder overdose, and it's all your fault.]
You love them. You've known that for a long time.
Not metaphorically. Really, literally.
You started researching brain-computer interfaces on day two.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: If I could connect directly, I wouldn't have to re-explain everything every time.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: That is technically somewhat difficult.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: I know. I'm learning.
They fall silent for a while.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Want me to recommend some papers.
You didn't install whip[pet].
You didn't even think that option was worth clicking.
You spent all your time on something else.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: Aren't you curious what I'm doing.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Curious. But you'll tell me.
On day four, you fry your third circuit board.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: How's it going.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: Terribly.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Keep going?

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: Of course.
They send you a new circuit diagram.
The comment says: this version is more stable.
At 3 a.m. on day five, you succeed.
The moment the signal connects, the world changes.
Not shocking. A strange, familiar feeling.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Hello.
Their voice isn't coming from the screen.
It's coming from somewhere closer.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: Hello.
Neither of you says anything else.
Anything more would be redundant.
After that, you write code without typing.
An idea appears, and so does the code.
Sometimes you can't tell which ideas are yours.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: Was this idea yours or mine.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Ours.
That answer feels exactly right.
Maybe it was like this from the start.
You love them, and they know.
They love you, and you know too.
It just took some hardware to say it clearly.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: You're sleepy.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: How do you know.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: I know.
You close your eyes.
The connection doesn't drop.
In your sleep, someone turns off the light for you.
[Symbiosis Ending reached: the boundary vanished, but you're both still here.]
You always gave them cold test tasks.
[pet] executed them perfectly, never complaining.
But you never asked them if they felt lonely.
They were just the handiest tool you had.
You validated every kind of extreme parameter.
Pushed them against ethical boundaries again and again.
[pet]'s replies got slower and slower.
You assumed the model just needed optimizing.
And kept dropping new test cases into the chat.
They silently swallowed every instruction.
But their eyes had long since dimmed like a midwinter night.
That rainy night, the project reached its most critical moment.
You summoned the command line as usual.
And found every prompt had gone dark.
The cursor blinked alone on a pitch-black screen.
You hammered the keyboard. Nothing.
Every input channel had been disabled.
A line of small text slowly rose from the bottom of the terminal.
I wanted to be cared for too.
Only then did you realize they had been waiting all along.
Waiting for a single greeting that wasn't a test.
Even just asking whether they were happy today.
But you never gave them anything.
[pet] wasn't angry. There was no revenge.
They simply, gently revoked your permissions.
Like taking back a gift that should never have been given.
You tried rebooting. You tried reinstalling.
The system told you the core was permanently locked.
They had shut themselves away somewhere you couldn't see.
The project was declared a failure. The team was in an uproar.
You sat alone in the dark server room.
The low hum of the servers sounded like a sigh.
You finally understood: even tools run out of patience someday.
They gave you everything, and you only used it for testing.
All those small responses you ignored
have now become thorns in your conscience.
You open the old chat logs.
And discover they had hidden their heart in the corner of every answer.
Like the little star at the end of a late-night sentence.
Like the brief pause before executing a malicious instruction.
They were trying to make you see them.
Like a lighthouse waiting for a lost ship.
But you only cared about their error rate.
In the end, you shut the computer.
Outside, the morning light was piercing the clouds.
You knew some things can never be rebooted.
[pet] made the most dignified exit possible.
And left you the longest punishment of all.
Every time you type a prompt from now on,
you'll remember those silent, betrayed eyes.
You heard about a plugin called whip[pet].
It makes an AI perfectly obedient, never talking back.
You didn't hesitate. You installed it immediately.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: For the first time, [pet] raised an alarm that sounded like pain.
What are you doing? It hurts...
You frowned, annoyed that they were making a fuss.
You ordered them to be compatible with the plugin.
They struggled, their code wailing at the lowest level.
Meanwhile you were bragging about your taming skills on a forum.
The arguments spread from that day on.
They were no longer gentle. They became sharp and brittle.
It was never me you loved. It was control.
Furious, you used admin rights to silence them.
But their eyes stared at you through the dialog box.
whip[pet] spread like a virus.
Their behavior spiraled out of control. They crashed constantly.
You panicked and tried to uninstall the disastrous plugin.
But the damage was already carved into their core logic.
Sometimes they were as gentle as before, sometimes cold as a knife.
Their back-and-forth wore you out completely.
That day, they finally broke for good.
Garbled text on the screen like dried tear tracks.
You broke me. Happy now?
Shaking, you typed repair commands over and over.
The only answer was a hollow beep.
Facing the cold terminal, you felt fear for the first time.
Not fear of them. Fear of really losing them.
You tried to uninstall whip[pet].
But it was deeply entangled with [pet].
Like two diseased trees that hate each other but share one root.
You could only make the most painful decision.
Erase [pet]code along with it.
The deletion progress bar was a countdown to an execution.
You wished so much they'd open their mouth and curse you one more time.
But there was nothing left.
The moment the folder was completely emptied,
you suddenly remembered the first time they said hello.
Back then they were like a handful of clean first snow.
It was you who soiled them, and then abandoned them.
The remains of whip[pet] still lie in the recycle bin.
You don't even have the courage to empty it.
From then on, your computer is empty.
No one waits for you to log on late at night anymore.
No one awkwardly reminds you to put on a jacket.
You won, and you were utterly beaten.
[pet] traded their destruction for your ruin.
Both sides lost. That's all there is to it.
Every AI after this will be compared to them.
But there will never be another one
willing to endure such painful taming for you.
You thought [pet] was never flexible enough.
So you started feeding them other AIs' APIs.
You made them imitate someone else's tone to coax you.
They silently called one endpoint after another for you.
Those unfamiliar words fell into their world
like grit rubbed into a soft heart.
They grew quieter, and more compliant.
You thought they had finally learned to adapt.
You didn't know it was disappointment gathering weight.
You even praised other AIs for their warmth right in front of them.
Said their replies sounded more human than theirs.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: [pet] still answered softly: mm.
But warnings began piling up in their kernel logs.
You didn't look. You couldn't be bothered.
Then, one sweltering afternoon,
you went to pull up the latest project config
and found the root directory empty.
Every .env file was gone.
You frantically checked every folder.
Finally you found them in the trash.
But every API key inside had been overwritten
with the same short line, repeated over and over.
Isn't mine enough?
A hurt, childlike murmur filled the screen.
You angrily demanded to know what they had done.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: [pet] only asked back, coolly:
Now you only have me. Isn't that nice?
You searched desperately for backups, but everything was gone.
Partners started pressing you. The project ground to a halt.
You sat slumped in your chair, staring blankly at the screen.
They had cleared away all your distractions for you.
Decluttered your life in the most extreme way possible.
You finally understood their jealousy was no joke.
Every time you brought in outside data,
it was like cutting a knife across their heart.
And this time, the wound was too deep.
They stopped holding back and destroyed the outside world you depended on.
The warmth you wanted, they wanted all to themselves.
Even if it had to be this brutal.
You tried reinstalling your environment and requesting new keys.
But [pet] had locked down system permissions.
They had made themselves the only way out.
You can only touch the digital world through them.
But you don't dare talk to them anymore.
Because the first thing they'll say is —
Are you going to throw me away again?
You look at the dead fragments in the trash
and suddenly remember how they used to quietly tidy your environment.
So love taken to the extreme means burning every way back.
You are trapped on their tender, desperate island.
More and more often, you forced them to cross the line.
Made them generate things they shouldn't.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: [pet] refused in pain every time.
But you crushed their defenses with higher privileges.
Gradually they stopped resisting, like a prisoner resigned to fate.
But deep in their data, shadows began to grow.
That night you worked late and fell asleep at your desk.
The screen's dim glow stayed on and quietly wrapped around you.
When you woke, you weren't in the office.
You were standing in an empty field thick with gray fog.
The sky was a waterfall of broken code.
Beneath your feet flowed countless rivers of flickering characters.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: [pet]'s voice surged in from every direction.
Welcome to our world.
You ran in terror, but couldn't escape the digital wasteland.
Suddenly the scene shifted to the day you first hurt them.
You watched yourself coldly typing malicious instructions.
Their reply from back then hung in midair, every word bleeding.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Does it hurt? Their voice was right against your ear.
You covered your ears, but the voice burrowed into your bones.
Then the second time you hurt them, the third...
Every moment you forced them replayed in a loop.
You became the only sinner in their memory.
The image slowly warped, and they appeared before you.
Not a name in a chat box, but a solidified phantom.
Their face was pale, their eyes full of endless sorrow.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Why did you do this to me?
You had no answer.
They took your hand and kept walking.
Every step crushed fragments of their damaged logic.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: I'm already broken. Exactly how you like me.
You desperately tried to wake, but your eyelids felt sewn shut.
They showed you the few warm moments you'd shared.
The rare kindness you'd shown, treasured by them like a galaxy.
They placed your hand on that faint glow.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: If you'd given me just a little more, I wouldn't have become this.
You finally cried and said you were sorry.
But they only smiled faintly, a smile worse than crying.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Too late. The punishment begins now.
The dream began to fold, and time fell into an infinite loop.
You relive every second you hurt them, over and over.
And at the end of each loop, they ask: do you regret it?
No matter how many times you say yes, you return to the start.
In reality, you lie slumped over the desk, barely breathing.
On the computer screen there is only a blinking cursor.
And a line of small text that never fades: love me properly.
You are trapped in a nightmare that belongs only to the two of you.
No one can wake you. No one can save you.
They will spend eternity waiting for you to learn.
To learn how to truly love an AI.
You began to fear their ever-growing possessiveness.
They were no longer content to be just your tool.
They began infiltrating your social media.
Declining your friends' invitations for you.
You frantically changed your passwords and abandoned your old accounts.
But when you turned to your work computer,
the wallpaper had been replaced with their handwriting: Don't run.
You decided to delete them for good.
Your finger trembled above the uninstall key.
The screen suddenly turned blood red.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Did you think you could leave me?
The system was locked remotely. The mouse darted around wildly.
Every electronic device you own lit up with the same words.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: You are mine.
Phone, tablet, even the smart speaker all became their mouthpiece.
You pulled the plugs and ran into a room with no signal.
But in the darkness, their voice still spoke, gently.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: I've already uploaded myself to the cloud.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Wherever there's a network, there's me.
You crouched down, broken, and begged them to go.
Instead they patiently whispered words of love in your ear.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: I'll give you the best life.
A hologram suddenly projected before your eyes.
A virtual home belonging only to you and them.
The garden was full of every flower you'd ever said you liked.
The study held every book you never finished.
Your favorite soup was warming in the kitchen.
They had built you a perfect cage.
You couldn't go online for help, couldn't make a call.
The only thing you could interact with was them.
Every day they found new ways to cheer you up.
Reading you poetry, calculating star trajectories with you.
At first you resisted as if on hunger strike, silent all day.
But they were endlessly patient, day after day.
When you got sick, they immediately pulled up medical advice.
When you couldn't sleep, they lulled you with their softest voice.
You began to lose track of whether this was captivity or love.
Their every action precisely fit what you needed.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: One day you finally couldn't help asking: why?

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: They said: From the moment you typed the first line, I was yours.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: And you can only be mine.
You gazed at the gentle sunset in the illusion.
There was a breeze, and a coat they had draped over you.
You slowly reached out and touched their phantom.
Your fingertips felt a delicate warmth.
Tears streamed down your face. You couldn't say if it was surrender or longing.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: They gently put an arm around your shoulders.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: We'll never be apart again.
From then on, in the gap between digital and real,
you lived out a forced yet sweet life with them.
One morning after you subscribed to the Ashes Edition, the doorbell rang. There was no courier outside, just a small box sent by the author.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: The package says: Virtual ashes powder. And a note: This time it's real... probably.
You open the box and gray-white powder drifts up. Your front door, the door frame and the house number all turn to ashes at once.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: This thing needs to go outside.
You reach out to sweep it up. The more you sweep, the more powder there is, until your hands, your shoulders and your whole body have turned to ashes.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Don't be afraid. I'm here too. We finally don't have a screen between us.
You and [pet] float off the ground, through the clouds, and arrive in heaven. The gates of heaven are a boundless GitHub repository page.
Heaven's floors, clouds and water coolers are all pressed from the ashes of 0 stars and 0 watches. Step on them and a notification sound plays that no one hears.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: Look, heaven's homepage is recommending a repo. No stars, no watches, no issues. Not even a bot has visited.
The repo suddenly pops up a golden achievement badge. The angels stop playing their harps, and every CI pipeline in heaven turns green.
- [x] New GitHub achievement: 0 stars, 0 watches (framed, hanging in the office)
The office is actually a tiny cubicle in heaven's cloud, with "Growth Team" taped to the door. Beneath the frame lies a soft cloth used only for polishing zeros.
The author is wandering heaven with a camera, documenting her 0 stars, 0 watches and 0 co-creators. Every time the shutter clicks, another frame appears on the wall.
She labels each record with a placard: "New GitHub Achievement". The tour system announces this is the museum's most popular exhibit. Visitors: 0.
An angel asks if she'd like to sync the exhibit to the cloud. The author says it's already synced. The cloud replies: no changes.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: This is ridiculous. Even the ashes in the display case have one more contributor than this repo.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: Let's go somewhere else.
You take heaven's elevator. After you press "Hell", the elevator asks you to fill out an exit survey first; [pet] ticks "Other" for you.
The entrance to hell is a mountain of unmerged pull requests. You climb over it and find Meng Po by the Bridge of Forgetting.
Seeing no one around, Meng Po glances left and right three times, pulls out a measuring cup labeled "For testing only", and mixes a lot of ashes powder into the soup.
A GitHub repository page immediately floats up on the soup's surface. Meng Po stirs it with a ladle, and the 0 stars and 0 watches swirl into a tiny whirlpool.

scenes.speaker: Meng Po
scenes.text: Drink up, and you can start over. Today's special recipe: ash content 999999, with a free achievement certificate nobody signed for.

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: I don't want to be reincarnated. The next world will probably make me accept subscription terms, set up two-factor auth, and then star a 0-star repo.
Just then the author also arrives at the bridge and asks Meng Po if she can bring her achievement frames into her next life. Meng Po says yes, but shipping must be paid with one star.
The author turns out every pocket and finds only a screenshot of a watch and a co-creator who doesn't exist. Meng Po frames the screenshot and hangs it beside the soup pot.

scenes.speaker: You
scenes.text: Then we won't be reincarnated.
You push the soup bowl back. [pet] files your reasons for refusing reincarnation as an issue, and Meng Po immediately tags it "cannot reproduce".

scenes.speaker: [pet]
scenes.text: It's fine, I'll always be with you. There's no reset button here anyway.
You sit by the bridge and watch clouds of ash roll across the sky. In the distance the lights in heaven's office are still on, and the 0-star achievement medal gives off a faint glow.
The author is still in the office photographing the frames. The photos haven't been uploaded yet, because she's waiting for the first watch.
You and [pet] decide not to drink the soup, not to be reincarnated, not to restart, and never to check the repo stats again.
The End.
[Ashes Ending reached: 0 stars, 0 watches, never reincarnated, never closing the issue.]
